settings.upc_help: Barcode scanning works without any key. Books are looked up on Open Library and records on Deezer and MusicBrainz. Games, films and other products are asked of UPCitemdb (no key, 100 a day, strongest on North American boxes) and Open Icecat (no key, strongest on European boxes: games, consoles, electronics, toys). Every barcode the forum resolves, or a member matches by hand, is kept, so it never needs asking twice. A paid UPCitemdb key only raises UPCitemdb's daily limit; most forums never need one.
settings.barcodes_help: Members can scan or type a barcode or ISBN to find what they are adding. Turned off, the Scan button goes, a number typed in the search box is searched as a title, and the forum asks no barcode service at all.
settings.barcodelookup_help: A paid service, asked after the free ones and before eBay for barcodes they miss. Plans start at about $99 a month for 5,000 answers; a look-up that finds nothing is not counted, and a free test key is offered on the same page. Curio reads only the product name (its images and descriptions belong to third parties and are never used), keeps a name for a day, and asks at most 200 times a day, 25 per member.
settings.eansearch_help: A paid database of about 1.3 billion barcodes, asked after barcodelookup.com and before eBay. Plans start at about €19 a month for 5,000 queries, with a €1 trial month of 100 (once per person); every query counts, found or not. Curio asks in the forum's language, keeps a name for a month and a miss for a week, and asks at most 200 times a day, 25 per member. Your token is shown in your EAN-Search account after sign-up.
settings.ebay_help: For barcodes UPCitemdb and Open Icecat don't know, a free eBay developer account lets Curio ask eBay, which lists almost every boxed product. Sign in (or join the eBay Developers Program), open Application Keys and create a Production keyset (any name). Beside the keyset, open Notifications and, under Marketplace Account Deletion, turn on the "Not persisting eBay data" exemption: Curio keeps only the product name it reads and the barcode, never listings, sellers or buyers. Copy the App ID and the Cert ID here. eBay is asked last, at most 1,000 times a day; its photos are not used.
settings.ebay_market_help: The eBay site whose listings name the barcode. By default it follows the forum's language (French → eBay France, German → eBay Germany, British English → eBay UK, otherwise eBay US).
settings.deepl_help: When Wikipedia has no description in a language, DeepL translates the English one. Free keys end in ":fx".
settings.max_upload_help: Photos are re-encoded as WebP and resized, so what is stored is much smaller than this.
settings.layout_help: How the Collections page shows each type.
settings.layout_compact: Compact tabs (one row of small buttons)
settings.type_color_help: With compact tabs, each type's colour can fill its tab or only colour its icon and name.
settings.type_color_text: On the icon and name only
settings.latest_help: A row on the Collections page with the latest progress members marked (completed, in progress…) and the latest ratings they gave, from collections the reader can see.
settings.hide_empty_label: Hide types with nothing in them
settings.hide_empty_help: Off by default, so the Collections page shows every switched-on type, as the Tags page shows every tag; an empty one invites a first collection. When on, only types holding something are shown (all of them while the forum has nothing yet).
settings.cover_fit_label: Covers that don't fit the frame
settings.cover_fit_help: Each type has a cover shape, so a collection's grid stays tidy. A cover of another shape (a 3:4 game box in a 2:3 frame) can be shown whole on a blurred copy of itself, whole on a plain background, or cropped to fill. A type whose shape matches its covers (Portrait 3:4 for game boxes) needs none of this.
settings.cover_fit_blur: Show whole on a blurred background
settings.cover_fit_plain: Show whole on a plain background
settings.shortcut_help: Where members find a link to their own collections.
settings.widget_help: Off by default. When on, the widget can be placed with Bespoke or FoF Forum Widgets (it first appears in FoF's right-hand column; move or remove it in FoF's layout editor).
settings.igdb_help: With a free Twitch developer app, game look-ups search IGDB: cover, developer, publisher, release date, platforms and genres. Register an application (any name; OAuth redirect URL http://localhost; category Application Integration), then copy its Client ID and make a New Secret. Without it, games are looked up through Marquee when it is installed.

types.heading: Collection types
types.help: Members pick a type for each collection. A type sets the cover shape, the details asked for, and where look-ups come from. Drag to change the order.
types.name: Name
types.color_help: A hex code such as #5b3fd1. Leave it blank to use the forum's colour.
types.needs_marquee: Film and TV search comes from Marquee, and game search from IGDB (set up in the settings above) or Marquee. Until it is installed, members of this type can still scan barcodes or add items by hand.
types.cards_help: Free, no key needed: Pokémon from TCGdex (in the reader's language where it has it), Magic from Scryfall, Yu-Gi-Oh! from YGOPRODeck. Set, card number, rarity and language fill the details with those names (set, number, rarity, language) when the type has them.
types.fields_help: What members fill in for each item. The first choice field is used for the breakdown and filter on collection pages (platform, format…).
types.review_link: Review link: shows “Read my review” beside the rating
types.translation_note: Titles and descriptions from look-ups arrive in each installed language by themselves (Wikidata and Wikipedia). Only the labels you write here need translating.
types.in_use: A type with collections cannot be deleted.
types.save_failed: The type could not be saved.
types.enabled_help: When off, members don't see this type and can't start a collection of it. Collections already made with it stay, seen only by their owners and moderators. Admins can still try it out.
types.progress_help: Each item can be marked Not started, In progress or Completed: a badge on the item and a filter on the collection page. Handy for a backlog of games, books or films.
types.import_help: Types travel as JSON files with their details and every language's labels. Importing adds them as new types.

types.import_failed: That file isn't a Curio types export.
